_about: Drafted lesson parts awaiting the teacher's approval (none at the moment: the 34 drafted 2026-10-28 were all approved that day and moved to PARTS.json) (meta/STUDENT_WORK_PLAN_2026-10.md, Phase 3), in PARTS.json's shape plus each lesson's status, why and concerns (what the teacher should decide). Nothing here is live: the builder reads only PARTS.json. tools/cas-ccps/check-parts-drafts.js builds every draft with the lesson builder; tools/cas-ccps/render-parts-drafts.js writes the teacher's copy of every lesson in parts, meta/LESSON_PARTS_2026-10.md. Approving a lesson moves its entry into PARTS.json and out of this file.
_across: **Text after the last part lands in the last part.** The builder gives each part the paragraphs from its "Part n:" to the next one, so a closing paragraph goes to the last part even when it is about an earlier one: 8175's "Submission: … paste into the submission box", 8177 notes such as "Your budget is confidential" (The Bottom Line), "Everything on a resume must be true" (The Final Whistle), "Do not contact any of these businesses" (The Sponsorship Negotiation), and the labeling rules in The NIL Deal and The Franchise Evolution. To do as each lesson is next edited: move each such line into the part it belongs to in the prompt file, and drop 8175's Submission line, which CAS replaces.

**"Add the link to this document" no longer fits a part whose work file is a Form, Slides or Sheet.** Until Phase 4 makes those the work files, a non-doc part is still a doc with the link pasted in, so the wording can stay for now; it changes with Phase 4.

**Parts that build on earlier parts.** Many later parts use an earlier part's work (a survey, a budget, a persona, a map). The student keeps every earlier part's doc, and Flow 2 now reads the earlier parts when it checks a later one (#316); some tasks may still want a line telling the student to bring the numbers forward.

**Live activities and role-plays.** Parts done in class with others (a negotiation, a role-play, an event) can only be checked through what the student writes about them, and a student who was absent can't do them. The teacher's unlock ("Open Part n now" on the Teacher Dashboard) is the way past one; the lessons below name each case.

**Optional competencies as primaries.** Where the teacher plan marks a competency "(Optional)" but it is the only fit for a part, the draft makes it that part's primary, so the student must meet it to go on (named in the lessons where it happens).
